official.deadline_note: The CTU Scholarships page publishes no application deadline, intake calendar or closing date. It describes a standing award procedure: obtain the agreement of your faculty, then submit the application through the International Office at your faculty to the Department of International Relations at the rectorate of CTU. Practical timing is therefore set by the faculty's own internal cycle and by the start of the semester the student asks the money for.
official.status_note: No application window or closing date is published. The page states a standing procedure under Act No. 111/1998 Sb., On Universities, section 91, paragraph (3), letter (b), open to foreign students enrolled at the relevant CTU faculty once that faculty has agreed to the application. The page was last changed by the rectorate's Department of International Relations on 19 September 2025.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The page publishes no wording on tuition fees for either track. The Master's award is described only as 'a contribution towards covering the costs for a stay in the Czech Republic up to an amount of CzK 10 000 per month'; the doctoral award is described as covering 'the basic scholarship awarded to students of doctoral study progammes and living costs in an amount up to CzK 16 000 per month'. No tuition waiver or fee reduction is mentioned.
benefits: Master's track: a contribution towards covering the costs for a stay in the Czech Republic up to an amount of CzK 10 000 per month
Doctoral track: covers the basic scholarship awarded to students of doctoral study progammes and living costs in an amount up to CzK 16 000 per month

Master's track: normally awarded for a period of 1 to 2 semesters; in the event of excellent study results it can be extended until the time corresponding to the standard length of the Master study programme

Doctoral track: awarded to an individual student for a period of 6-12 months; in the event of excellent work outcomes it can be extended until the maximum time corresponding to the standard length of the study programme
Financed equally from the scholarship fund of the rectorate of CTU and the scholarship fund of the relevant faculty or part of the university
eligibility: Master's track: intended for foreign students who wish to take a Master study programme at CTU and who display qualities that entitle them to the award of this scholarship

Doctoral track: intended for foreign doctoral students who are capable of doing scientific work and studying on a doctoral programme in English language at CTU in Prague, and who display qualities that entitle them to the award of this scholarship
The student is enrolled as a foreign student at the relevant faculty of CTU
Not eligible: Erasmus students at CTU
Not eligible: Erasmus Mundus students at CTU
Not eligible: Exchange students at CTU
Not eligible: CTU foreign students receiving a government scholarship

Submit the application through the International Office at your faculty to the Department of International Relations at the rectorate of CTU, on the form available on the web pages of the rectorate of CTU

official.application_route: Secure your faculty's agreement first, then submit the official CTU scholarship application form via your faculty's International Office to the Department of International Relations at the rectorate of CTU - you do not apply directly to the rectorate yourself.
official.citizenship_residency: The award is for foreign students; the Master's track requires the student to be enrolled as a foreign student at the relevant CTU faculty, and the doctoral track requires study on a doctoral programme in English language at CTU in Prague.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scholarship is intended exclusively for foreign students (foreign students on Master study programmes and foreign doctoral students on English-language doctoral programmes at CTU in Prague). Erasmus, Erasmus Mundus, exchange students and CTU foreign students on a government scholarship are excluded.
official.research_requirement: Doctoral track: the applicant must be capable of doing scientific work; the individual study plan under Art. 30 point 1 of the study and examination regulations is binding and forms part of the application; and one outcome of the study stay must be results published in an internationally reviewed journal or an application submitted for an international grant, reported to the faculty's Science and Research Department no later than three months after the study stay ends.
official.duration: Master's track: normally 1 to 2 semesters, extendable on excellent study results until the time corresponding to the standard length of the Master study programme. Doctoral track: 6-12 months, extendable on excellent work outcomes until the maximum time corresponding to the standard length of the study programme.
official.description: CTU awards a scholarship to foreign students who wish to take a Master study programme at the Czech Technical University in Prague and display qualities that entitle them to the award, and to foreign doctoral students capable of doing scientific work who study on a doctoral programme in English language at CTU in Prague. The Master's award is a contribution towards covering the costs for a stay in the Czech Republic of up to CzK 10 000 per month for one to two semesters, while the doctoral award covers the basic scholarship for doctoral study programmes and living costs of up to CzK 16 000 per month for six to twelve months. Both are financed equally from the scholarship fund of the rectorate of CTU and the scholarship fund of the relevant faculty, and are awarded under Act No. 111/1998 Sb., On Universities, section 91, paragraph (3), letter (b).
official.program_type: University scholarship for foreign students on Master's and doctoral study programmes at CTU, awarded under Act No. 111/1998 Sb., On Universities, section 91, paragraph (3), letter (b)
official.english_requirement: Doctoral track: the applicant must be studying on a doctoral programme in English language at CTU in Prague. The published rules state no minimum English test score for either track; programme admission requirements are handled separately through the faculty's doctoral admission procedure.

verification.notes: Read the awarding body's own CTU Scholarships page (international.cvut.cz, maintained by the rectorate's Department of International Relations, last changed 19.09.2025) plus the official CTU scholarship application form it links and the CTU PhD Programmes in English page. Both track amounts (CZK 10 000 and CZK 16 000 per month), the periods, the exclusion list, the funding split and the application route were taken verbatim from those pages; no aggregator or search-snippet value was used.

applicant_utility.summary: Treat this as a top-up, not a scholarship that will fund your degree: at the published ceiling it tops out at CZK 10 000 per month on the Master's track and CZK 16 000 per month on the doctoral track, and nothing in it touches tuition. You cannot apply on your own - the first step is persuading your own CTU faculty to agree to sponsor you, and the paperwork then travels from your faculty's International Office to the rectorate, so your faculty's internal calendar is the real deadline. If you already hold any other scholarship, a Czech government scholarship, or you came through Erasmus, Erasmus Mundus or an exchange programme, this route is closed to you. Doctoral applicants get the better deal and the harder conditions: a binding individual study plan, and a publication or grant application you must be able to show the faculty within three months of finishing your stay.
applicant_utility.best_fit: An already-enrolled foreign Master's or English-taught doctoral student at CTU who has a supportive faculty and needs breathing room on rent and food, rather than someone looking for full funding to come to Prague.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm with your faculty's International Office that your faculty will agree to sponsor a CTU scholarship application and ask which internal cut-off they work to, since the rectorate publishes none
Check you are not simultaneously holding any other scholarship or a Czech government scholarship, and that you did not enter CTU via Erasmus, Erasmus Mundus or an exchange programme
Map out the exact months you are asking the money for in dd.mm.yy-dd.mm.yy form, and agree the monthly amount and total with the Vice-Dean for International Relations before you fill in the form

Draft the credit-by-credit list of subjects you intend to take at CTU with codes, semesters and credits, including the ones you have already passed in your first year if you are asking for an extension
Doctoral applicants: get your individual study plan (Art. 30 point 1) finalised and agreed with your supervisor first, because it forms part of the application itself
Decide which address correspondence should go to and give one stable email plus a postal address you will still check after your stay ends
common_rejection_risks: Losing eligibility mid-study: the award can lapse after the first semester if you fail to meet the study requirements in your study and examination regulations, so a weak first semester costs you the money and not just a grade

Missing the extension gate on the Master's track entirely because not every accredited first-year course was completed within the recommended time plan - that lapses your entitlement to reapply, not just this round
Being disqualified on a technicality: Erasmus, Erasmus Mundus, exchange status, a Czech government scholarship, or any other scholarship you are already holding are all hard exclusions
Applying without your faculty's prior agreement, which leaves the rectorate's Department of International Relations with nothing it can act on
Doctoral applicants who treat the publication or grant-application outcome as an afterthought and then cannot produce the copy for the final report within the three-month deadline
Assuming the full CZK 10 000 or CZK 16 000 will be paid - the rules say 'up to', and the actual monthly figure is written into the faculty's declaration
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees in full, because the published coverage is limited to a stay-cost contribution (and on the doctoral track the basic doctoral scholarship plus living costs). You would also still be covering your own accommodation deposit and rent above the stipend, Czech health insurance, visa and residence-permit costs, travel to and from Prague, and study materials. Note that Prague halls of residence are a separate application from this scholarship.
document_audit: The application form asks for your nationality exactly as printed in your passport - a mismatch between passport, enrolment record and the form is an easy way to stall the file
The form contains a declaration about your health and physical ability to study at CTU, so it is not a purely administrative document
The monthly amount and total sum are entered by your Vice-Dean for International Relations, not by you - if you fill in your own figure the form has to be redone
Doctoral applications must carry the individual study plan as an attachment, so it needs to be agreed and dated before you submit
Any correspondence address you give has to still work months later, because the doctoral track's final report obligation only closes three months after your stay ends
alerts: There is no published deadline, which is not the same as being open all year - agreement from your faculty is the gate, and faculties have their own internal cut-offs tied to semester starts
The award can be withdrawn after the first semester if your study results slip, so it is renewable in practice only while you keep passing everything on schedule
Holding any other scholarship at the same time is a disqualifier, so decide which single award you want before you apply

Doctoral applicants take on a reporting obligation that continues after the money stops: the publication or grant application must go to the faculty's Science and Research Department within three months of finishing the stay
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You agree the terms with your Vice-Dean for International Relations and fill in the official CTU form, your faculty's International Office forwards the application to the rectorate's Department of International Relations, and the vice-rector decides on the recommendation of the commission of vice-deans for international relations.
